title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on p.25 Grothendieck 'starts everything over' with a new primitive notion. A contrée C consists of a set L of 'lieux' (places) together with a set of figures. Each figure F is a set of subsets of L, called its strates. The support |F| is the union of its strata; the transcription of p.25 reads 'nombre', but the use here shows |F| is a subset of L. Axiom Cont 1 says the empty figure and the one-point figures {{x}} exist.

This page states axiom Cont 2. F is ordered by inclusion. For a stratum X in F, set dX = union of the strata Y in F with Y strictly contained in X (the boundary) and X° = X minus dX (the 'open stratum defined by X'). The axiom has two parts:
(i) X° is nonempty for every X (a marginal note calls this 'admissibility');
(ii) for X, Y in F, X∩Y is the union of the strata Z in F with Z ≤ X and Z ≤ Y. In words: every place lying in two closed strata lies in a stratum contained in their intersection.

Corollary: the map X ↦ X° from F to P(|F|) is a bijection of F onto the set of classes of an equivalence relation on |F|. Equivalently, X ≠ Y ⇔ X°∩Y° = ∅, and the X° partition |F|. He notes that this is in fact equivalent to Cont 2. He then names this a 'partition stratifiée' of |F|, whose closed strata are the X in F.

A crossed-out start defines when two figures F, G are 'compatible': |F|∩|G| should be saturated for the equivalence relations of both, i.e. their stratifications should match on the overlap. Next page: sub-figures are the down-closed (saturated) subsets of the poset F. Mere inclusion F' ⊂ F is not enough.

In modern terms, a figure is a finite closed stratification of a subset of L satisfying the frontier condition. Each closed stratum is the union of the open strata below it. The stratum map |F| → F is order-compatible, so |F| is stratified over the poset F. A contrée is thus a set equipped with a class of admissible finite stratifications, playing the role of a topology. This is a foundational step in Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at an axiomatic 'analysis situs' / tame topology.
errors: The corollary and the claimed equivalence with Cont 2 implicitly need F to be finite, or at least well-founded under inclusion. This is needed so that every x in |F| lies in a minimal stratum, which gives x ∈ X°, and so that X = union of Z° over Z ≤ X. Finiteness is not stated on this page, though it is presumably intended.
In the displayed formula the transcription reads 'F_Z'. The intended term is clearly just Z; the subscript appears to be a slip or a struck-out mark.

With finiteness the proofs go through. Disjointness: if x ∈ X°∩Y°, the Z ≤ X,Y containing x must equal X and Y. Converse: x ∈ X gives x ∈ Z° for some Z ≤ X, and uniqueness of the class gives Z ≤ Y. No genuine mathematical error.

ideas.what: Space axiomatized by a set of places plus a class of admissible finite stratifications ('figures') instead of open sets
ideas.modern_name: abstract stratified sets / tame-topology foundations; loosely akin to o-minimal structures (class of admissible definable sets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology programme: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984); o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 calls for tame topology and stratified structures, but this 'contrée/lieux/figures/strates' axiomatics is unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: Open stratum X° = X minus the union of smaller closed strata; nonemptiness ('admissibility'); intersection axiom equivalent to the X° partitioning |F|
ideas.modern_name: frontier condition for a closed stratification; stratification over a poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather (stratified spaces); poset-stratified formulation: e.g. Lurie (HA App. A), Treumann, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka

ideas.what: Compatibility of two stratifications on the overlap of their supports (crossed out)

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins an axiomatics in which a 'space' (contrée) is a set of places with a family of admissible finite stratifications. The figures are subject to axioms 'to be extracted later' and to a compatibility relation between figures. This is a foundational draft of the tame topology promised in the Esquisse, apparently never completed or published.
missed.quote: Partition stratifiée de |F| : p.ex. les X∈F
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a stratification-first alternative to o-minimal or point-set foundations for tame topology. It could be compared with current poset-stratified and exit-path approaches. The page itself contains only elementary definitions, so its interest is mainly historical.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is an elementary and correct formulation of the frontier condition for finite closed stratifications. The historical interest lies in its role as part of an unpublished axiomatic 'analysis situs' (contrées/figures), but this page alone contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Displayed formula: 'X∩Y = ∪_{Z∈F, Z≤X,Y} Z'. The 'F_Z' is a misreading of Z, which carries an underline or strike mark.
First line: 'dX*' has a struck-out asterisk; read 'dX = ∪_{Y∈F_{<X}} Y'.
Margin note reads roughly 'la condition que les X° soient non vides se dit «admissibilité»'.
On p.25, 'Le nombre des strates de F est appelé le support' should almost certainly read 'La réunion des strates', since |F| is used as a subset of L here.
